Source: https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/tensorrt-rtx/latest/inference-library/runtime-api.html

Using the Native Runtime API
This tutorial demonstrates how to build a TensorRT-RTX engine and run inference programmatically using the C++ or Python API. The example uses a simple convolutional neural network to illustrate the core workflow.
Note
The native API is intended for advanced use cases where you need fine-grained control over network construction. Most users should use the [ONNX-based workflow](<https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/tensorrt-rtx/latest/getting-started/build-your-first-engine.html#build-your-first-engine>) instead.
The workflow has two phases:
Build : Define a network, configure the builder, and serialize the engine to a file
Infer : Deserialize the engine, allocate GPU memory, and execute inference
Build the Engine
Define a simple convolution network and serialize it to an engine file.
C++ Listing 4 Build the engine (C++)
1 #include "NvInfer.h" 2 #include <cuda_runtime.h> 3 #include <fstream> 4 #include <iostream> 5 #include <memory> 6 #include <vector> 7 8 using namespace nvinfer1 ; 9 10 // Minimal logger implementation 11 class Logger : public ILogger { 12 void log ( Severity severity , const char * msg ) noexcept override { 13 if ( severity <= Severity :: kWARNING ) std :: cout << msg << std :: endl ; 14 } 15 } gLogger ; 16 17 void buildEngine ( const char * fileName ) { 18 auto builder = createInferBuilder ( gLogger ); 19 auto network = builder -> createNetworkV2 ( 0U ); 20 21 // Input tensor of shape {1, 1, 3, 3} 22 auto input = network -> addInput ( "input" , DataType :: kFLOAT , Dims4 { 1 , 1 , 3 , 3 }); 23 24 // Convolution weights: 3x3 kernel, 1 input channel, 1 output channel 25 std :: vector < float > weightValues ( 9 , 1.f ); 26 std :: vector < float > biasValues ( 1 , 0.f ); 27 Weights W { DataType :: kFLOAT , weightValues . data (), 9 }; 28 Weights B { DataType :: kFLOAT , biasValues . data (), 1 }; 29 30 auto conv = network -> addConvolutionNd ( * input , 1 , DimsHW { 3 , 3 }, W , B ); 31 conv -> setStrideNd ( Dims2 { 1 , 1 }); 32 33 // Mark network output 34 auto output = conv -> getOutput ( 0 ); 35 output -> setName ( "output" ); 36 network -> markOutput ( * output ); 37 38 // Build and serialize 39 auto config = builder -> createBuilderConfig (); 40 config -> setMemoryPoolLimit ( MemoryPoolType :: kWORKSPACE , 1ULL << 30 ); 41 auto engine = builder -> buildSerializedNetwork ( * network , * config ); 42 43 // Save to file 44 std :: ofstream out ( fileName , std :: ios :: binary ); 45 out . write ( static_cast < const char *> ( engine -> data ()), engine -> size ()); 46 out . close (); 47 48 // Clean up 49 // Note: While this example uses manual cleanup for clarity, 50 // production code should use smart pointers, such as std::unique_ptr 51 // to ensure proper resource management. 52 delete engine ; 53 delete network ; 54 delete config ; 55 delete builder ; 56 }
Python Listing 5 Build the engine (Python)
1 import tensorrt_rtx as trt_rtx 2 import numpy as np 3 4 GLOBAL_LOGGER = trt_rtx . Logger ( trt_rtx . Logger . WARNING ) 5 6 def build_engine ( file_name ): 7 builder = trt_rtx . Builder ( GLOBAL_LOGGER ) 8 network = builder . create_network ( 0 ) 9 10 # Input tensor of shape (1, 1, 3, 3) 11 input_t = network . add_input ( 12 name = "input" , dtype = trt_rtx . float32 , shape = ( 1 , 1 , 3 , 3 )) 13 14 # Convolution: 3x3 kernel, 1 output channel 15 w = np . full (( 1 , 1 , 3 , 3 ), 1.0 , dtype = np . float32 ) 16 b = np . zeros ( 1 , dtype = np . float32 ) 17 conv = network . add_convolution_nd ( 18 input = input_t , num_output_maps = 1 , 19 kernel_shape = ( 3 , 3 ), kernel = w , bias = b ) 20 conv . stride_nd = ( 1 , 1 ) 21 22 # Mark output 23 conv . get_output ( 0 ) . name = "output" 24 network . mark_output ( conv . get_output ( 0 )) 25 26 # Build and serialize 27 config = builder . create_builder_config () 28 config . set_memory_pool_limit ( trt_rtx . MemoryPoolType . WORKSPACE , 1 << 30 ) 29 host_mem = builder . build_serialized_network ( network , config ) 30 31 with open ( file_name , "wb" ) as f : 32 f . write ( host_mem )
Run Inference
Load the serialized engine, allocate device memory, run inference, and read back the result.
C++ 1 void performInference ( const char * fileName , const std :: vector < float >& inputData ) { 2 // Note: Error handling omitted for brevity. Production code should 3 // check return values and handle CUDA errors appropriately. 4 auto runtime = createInferRuntime ( gLogger ); 5 6 // Deserialize engine from file 7 std :: ifstream is ( fileName , std :: ios :: binary ); 8 is . seekg ( 0 , is . end ); 9 size_t nbBytes = is . tellg (); 10 is . seekg ( 0 , is . beg ); 11 std :: vector < uint8_t > data ( nbBytes ); 12 is . read ( reinterpret_cast < char *> ( data . data ()), nbBytes ); 13 is . close (); 14 15 auto engine = runtime -> deserializeCudaEngine ( data . data (), nbBytes ); 16 auto execContext = engine -> createExecutionContext (); 17 18 // Allocate device memory 19 void * bindings [ 2 ]; 20 size_t inputNbBytes = inputData . size () * sizeof ( float ); 21 size_t outputNbBytes = 1 * sizeof ( float ); 22 cudaMalloc ( & bindings [ 0 ], inputNbBytes ); 23 cudaMalloc ( & bindings [ 1 ], outputNbBytes ); 24 25 // Copy input to device 26 cudaMemcpy ( bindings [ 0 ], inputData . data (), inputNbBytes , cudaMemcpyHostToDevice ); 27 28 // Bind input/output addresses by tensor name (replaces deprecated executeV2 binding-array pattern) 29 const char * inputName = engine -> getIOTensorName ( 0 ); 30 const char * outputName = engine -> getIOTensorName ( 1 ); 31 execContext -> setTensorAddress ( inputName , bindings [ 0 ]); 32 execContext -> setTensorAddress ( outputName , bindings [ 1 ]); 33 34 // Run inference asynchronously on a CUDA stream 35 cudaStream_t stream ; 36 cudaStreamCreate ( & stream ); 37 execContext -> enqueueV3 ( stream ); 38 cudaStreamSynchronize ( stream ); 39 cudaStreamDestroy ( stream ); 40 41 // Copy result back to host 42 float result ; 43 cudaMemcpy ( & result , bindings [ 1 ], outputNbBytes , cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost ); 44 std :: cout << "Result = " << result << std :: endl ; 45 46 // Clean up 47 // Note: Production code should use smart pointers and RAII patterns 48 // for automatic resource management. Error handling for CUDA calls 49 // should also be implemented. 50 cudaFree ( bindings [ 0 ]); 51 cudaFree ( bindings [ 1 ]); 52 delete execContext ; 53 delete engine ; 54 delete runtime ; 55 }
Python 1 import numpy as np 2 import pycuda.driver as cuda 3 import pycuda.autoprimaryctx # Use autoprimaryctx, not autoinit 4 5 def perform_inference ( file_name , input_data ): 6 runtime = trt_rtx . Runtime ( GLOBAL_LOGGER ) 7 8 with open ( file_name , "rb" ) as f : 9 engine = runtime . deserialize_cuda_engine ( f . read ()) 10 11 exec_context = engine . create_execution_context () 12 13 # Allocate device memory 14 d_input = cuda . mem_alloc ( input_data . nbytes ) 15 output_data = np . empty (( 1 ,), dtype = np . float32 ) 16 d_output = cuda . mem_alloc ( output_data . nbytes ) 17 18 # Bind input/output addresses by tensor name (replaces deprecated execute_v2 binding-list pattern) 19 input_name = engine . get_tensor_name ( 0 ) 20 output_name = engine . get_tensor_name ( 1 ) 21 exec_context . set_tensor_address ( input_name , int ( d_input )) 22 exec_context . set_tensor_address ( output_name , int ( d_output )) 23 24 # Copy input to device and run inference asynchronously on a CUDA stream 25 cuda . memcpy_htod ( d_input , input_data ) 26 stream = cuda . Stream () 27 exec_context . execute_async_v3 ( stream . handle ) 28 stream . synchronize () 29 30 # Copy result back to host 31 cuda . memcpy_dtoh ( output_data , d_output ) 32 33 # Clean up 34 d_input . free () 35 d_output . free () 36 37 return output_data
For thread-safety rules, buffer lifetime contracts, object lifetimes, and other runtime concepts, refer to [How TensorRT-RTX Works](<https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/tensorrt-rtx/latest/architecture/how-trt-rtx-works.html#works>) .
